answer: A falcon-fast agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake at its inlet to the market, like a bond held in escrow. The stake is slashed if the agent cheats or floods the network with fake peers, and honest agents get it back at the zenith of a clean run. An attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand stakes, so the cost of a Sybil attack grows linearly with every fake it creates, while honest agents pay nothing beyond a temporary lockup.
